correctness.rationale: The return mean u solves u''+b2 u' = −1 with u(1)=0 and the stated scale-speed derivative; in the far negative tail the scale-speed ratio is at most 1/(c2 |x|) by integrating the dissipativity bound between y≤x and x. Thus u grows at most logarithmically there and (b1−b2)u' is bounded on x≤1, justifying the stopped Dynkin and renewal computations, whose success probability is positive. They give M_r−u(0)=N_r/p_r exactly. From |b1(x)|≤L|x|, a Gronwall bound by the Brownian running maximum gives the exponentially small short-time probability of hitting 1 and all needed moment bounds; comparison to sqrt(2)B_t in L1 gives E X_t^+=sqrt(t/pi)+O(t^(3/2)), and Itô gives E X_t²=2t+O(t²). Killing and fixed-neighborhood localization contribute errors smaller than every power after Laplace weighting. Near zero h(x)=x^+/S2+O(|x|³), so p_r=1/(2 S2 sqrt(r))+O(r^(−3/2)). With delta=b1'(0)−b2'(0), u''(0)=−1 and symmetry of unrestricted search eliminates odd terms, giving N_r=−2 delta r^(−2)+O(r^(−3)). Dividing gives the sign, factor 4 and O(r^(−5/2)) remainder in the claimed normalization; the exact identity gives equality when the drifts coincide. The finite mesh file was inspected, not executed or used as a continuum certificate.

originality.rationale: Pass for the quantified correction for arbitrary odd, smooth, globally Lipschitz and strongly confining drift pairs, not for the known plateau or the general renewal identity. A catalogue result gives exactly the exponential-clock OU specialization, but its arbitrary-clock generality does not cover nonlinear drifts. The general published renewal formula identifies the stopped-cycle ratio; it does not expose the signed drift discrepancy, parity cancellation or expansion of the ratio. The harmonic paper and free/harmonic plateau do not imply the nonlinear theorem.
